business_scope.primary_industry_name: GPS-Sealed Bonded Road Feeder Service for International Airports

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Marshall Islands is not a Hague Apostille Convention party)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against RMI domestic sanctions lists, United Nations Security Council consolidated lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, and enhanced PEP screening for shareholders, directors, beneficial owners and authorized signatories. Customer due diligence must include identity verification, source of funds/source of wealth assessment, risk-based monitoring, and adverse media/integrity checks. For this low-risk standard tier, simplified due diligence may apply only after positive identification and absence of sanctions/PEP hits; filing of a SAR to the RMI Financial Intelligence Unit is required on any suspicious transaction attempt.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Companies Registry Online Name Search and Reservation Portal (administered through the RMI Registrar of Corporations and licensed registered agents)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official system of records is English. Names may be submitted in English/Latin script; non-English names must be transliterated into a Latin-script version. The name must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing RMI domestic or nonresident corporation, limited partnership, limited liability partnership, or reserved name. Only the English/Latin script version is accepted for registry filing; local script names are not recognized for corporate identifiers.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name reservation or incorporation name is rejected, the applicant may, within 14 days from notice of rejection, file a written administrative appeal with the RMI Registrar of Corporations via the licensed registered agent. The appeal must set out the proposed name, the statutory or regulatory provision allegedly violated, and arguments for distinguishability or permitted use. The Registrar shall issue a written determination within 21 business days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the RMI High Court within 30 days of the denial, or resubmit the name with a consent letter from the relevant competent authority where the objection involves a sensitive token subject to ministerial licensing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office accepted for the non-resident Business Corporation structure. No physical presence or staff is required in the Marshall Islands. However, a licensed RMI registered agent must maintain a physical registered office address in the Marshall Islands, receive service of process, and maintain corporate records. The use of a virtual business address locally without a licensed registered agent is not permissible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for UBO piercing triggered by risk signals; quantified annual unannounced on-site physical inspection risk estimated at 5–7% for non-resident holding or transport-service vehicle entities with no active RMI-derived revenue. Inspection likelihood rises to approximately 20% if the entity applies for a customs-bonded license, operates through RMI ports, or is selected in a regulatory sample. All inspections are coordinated through the registered agent except where a judicial or FATF-style urgent order exists.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act, as amended (Title 27 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code), including incorporation, corporate governance, registered agent, and non-resident domestic corporation provisions
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Majuro; filings effected through licensed registered agents
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation filed under the Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required; the Articles of Incorporation may authorize shares at any par value or without par value. Escrow account rules are not applicable in the Marshall Islands non-resident corporation regime; the company must, however, maintain sufficient funding for fleet acquisition, customs bond requirements, and insurance.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the Corporation hereby accepts the share subscriptions set forth in the accompanying Subscription Agreement and issues the corresponding shares; adopts the registered office located in Majuro and confirms the registered agent; appoints the officers listed in the Officer Consent, with authority to open bank accounts, execute leases, and negotiate customs-bonded contracts; directs the President to maintain the Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws as the governing instruments; and authorizes all necessary steps to secure the industrial license, environmental assessment, and civil-defense clearances for the GPS-sealed bonded road feeder truck fleet. Any officer is further authorized to sign, file, and deliver all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Registered Agent Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, RMI – Online Name Reservation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name in English, including the required corporate suffix, and evidence of any trademark right to the name. Engage a licensed Marshall Islands registered agent who will accept service of process. Pay the name reservation fee and obtain a name availability certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized appointment of resident registered agent
Identification details of incorporators and initial directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried, provide an alternative name list or submit a distinctiveness explanation; re-file within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, through licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute and notarize the Articles of Incorporation and file them with the Registrar. Include authorized share capital, par value provisions, registered office street address, registered agent identity, corporate purpose, and limitations if any. Submit the filing fee by bank wire to the registry account or electronic payment rail accepted by the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Executed and notarized Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any clerical deficiency through a formal correction filing or notice of withdrawal and resubmission; respond to the Registrar's deficiency letter within 30 calendar days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Registered Agent Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations and licensed registered agent in Majuro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a Statement of Registered Office and Registered Agent and lodge it with the Registrar. The registered office must be a physical street address, not a post office box. The registered agent must sign a written acceptance of appointment and undertake to receive process on behalf of the corporation.
required_dossiers: Statement of Registered Office and Registered Agent
Proof of physical office address such as lease or tenancy document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the appointment is rejected, submit an amended statement naming a new registered agent or corrected office address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Board Meeting and Corporate Governance Adoption
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial directors of the corporation; corporate secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the initial directors. Adopt bylaws, elect officers, approve share subscriptions and issuance, and pass the pro forma first board resolution. Transcribe minutes in English and retain them in the corporate records. Ensure all officer consents and share subscription payment evidence are placed on file.
required_dossiers: First board meeting minutes or unanimous consent in lieu of meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director cannot attend and quorum is challenged, execute a unanimous written consent in lieu of a meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation Issuance and Registry Record Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, verify the company registration number, legal status, and registered details. Request certified copies of the Articles of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing for use in bank account opening and customs license procedures.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the issued certificate contains a typographical error, apply to the Registrar for a certificate of correction under the Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Customs, and Physical Licensing Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Customs and Revenue Service, Licensing Division; RMI Environmental Protection Agency; Civil Defense Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the customs bonded road feeder carrier license application. Provide a customs bond guarantee sufficient for the cargo and transit exposure, GPS-seal supplier contracts, vehicle registration and fleet lists, yard lease, fire safety clearance, structural load certificate, and environmental registration notice. Obtain the operational license before commencing bonded truck fleet movements.
required_dossiers: Fire safety and structural clearance certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, address customs bond insufficiency, amend the GPS-seal security protocol, or supplement environmental information within 15 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Marshall Islands Customs and Revenue Service, Licensing Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Customs Bonded Road Feeder Carrier License

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Agency of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI-EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Category II) – Environmental Compliance Notice; full EIA Report is required only if the fleet terminal refueling capacity or maintenance facility exceeds prescribed thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Fleet washwater and oil-water separator discharge must not exceed 15 mg/L oil and grease; waste solvents and used GPS-seal cleaning effluent must be removed by licensed hazardous waste handlers; truck diesel engines must comply with RMI-EPA clean air emission limits on particulate matter and sulfur dioxide; no untreated wastewater may be discharged to municipal storm drains or soil.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance from the Marshall Islands Fire and Emergency Services for the fueling depot and truck yard; structural load certificate for any docking bay or cargo warehouse; Occupational Health and Safety clearance from the RMI Ministry of Health for workplace conditions, driver fatigue management, and hazardous goods handling.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Marshall Islands Revenue and Customs Administration (RICA), Ministry of Finance, Banking and Customs; operational single-window portal is UNCTAD ASYCUDA World for customs and the RICA Taxpayer Portal for any voluntary tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-Resident Business Corporations (BCs) incorporated under the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act (BCA) 1990 are statutorily exempt from Marshall Islands income tax, withholding tax, and social security taxes. No TIN or tax registration is required for pure offshore service income. Procedure for a foreign-owned BC operating a customs bonded truck fleet: (1) obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and good-standing certificate from the Office of the Associate Registrar of Corporations; (2) file a Customs Bonded Carrier / Bonded Transit Registration with RICA in ASYCUDA World to secure duty suspension for feeder movements; (3) register as an Importer/Exporter with RICA and obtain the RICA customs numeric identifier; (4) if employing local drivers or staff, register as an employer with the Marshall Islands Social Security Administration (MINSA) and obtain a MINSA employer number; (5) no other national tax TIN is issued because no VAT/GST or income tax regime applies to non-resident entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists because the RMI imposes no corporate income tax. The BCA enables a BC to perfect statutory tax-exempt status by electing non-resident status under Section 98 of the BCA and maintaining no local-source revenue. For customs bonded operations, an election may be filed to operate as a licensed bonded carrier under the Customs Tariff Act 2004; no other treasury or fiscal elections apply.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Customs Import Duty and Selective Excise Tariff (no VAT/GST/sales-and-use tax system in force)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable - no VAT registration threshold exists in the RMI. Any person importing commercial goods or operating a bonded facility, including a GPS-sealed bonded road feeder fleet serving an international airport, must register with RICA and hold the applicable customs bond irrespective of turnover. Official currency is USD; no separate local currency code applies to the RMI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: ASYCUDA World is the sole mandatory clearance platform for all customs declarations, bonded transit manifests, and duty-suspension controls. No national real-time fiscal e-invoicing clearance, XML invoicing schema, or digital stamping mandate applies to domestic commercial invoices. Bonded feeder trucks must transmit GPS seal events and transit updates through the ASYCUDA transit module; invoices and supporting transport records must be retained for 5 years under the BCA record-keeping obligation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: No VAT/GST zero-rating mechanics exist because the RMI has no such tax. For customs duty purposes, goods moved from Amata Kabua International Airport to a licensed bonded facility by the bonded truck fleet qualify for duty suspension when the following criteria are met: valid Bonded Carrier Permit; ASYCUDA World in-transit manifest accepted by Customs; unbroken GPS seal with continuous tracking from air waybill release to bonded warehouse receipt; and physical inspection the seal record matches the Cargo Manifest. Export shipments leave the RMI customs territory without duty, and bonded transport services to non-resident airlines are wholly outside the RMI tax net.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (filed via ASYCUDA World)
Bill of Lading / Master and House Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate for exported goods proceeds when repatriation is required
Customs Bonded Carrier Permit and Bonded Transit Manifest
GPS Seal Log with continuous location data
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or erroneous claims of duty suspension or export exemption trigger retrospective liquidation of the full duty, a penalty of up to 100% of the duty evaded, forfeiture of the bonded vehicles and cargo under the Customs Tariff Act 2004, and criminal fines up to USD 5,000 and/or imprisonment up to 12 months for false declarations. RICA conducts risk-based audits of transit times, seal-break events, and GPS integrity; any seal interference without prior Customs authorization voids the duty suspension and renders the entire cargo immediately duty-paid.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Office of the Banking Commissioner of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (Ministry of Finance) as issuer of banking licences and prudential regulator; the RMI maintains no domestic central bank, with the US Federal Reserve serving as the de facto monetary authority because the US dollar is the sole legal tender under the Compact of Free Association.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full de jure and de facto convertibility: the RMI imposes no current-account or capital-account exchange controls, imposes no statutory withholding or approval gate on profit, dividend, loan-repayment, or share-liquidation remittances to non-resident shareholders, and operates entirely in USD. Residual remittance friction is confined to bank-level AML/KYC and correspondent-bank de-risking practices rather than to any FX-control regulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. The RMI enacts no export-proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for service-export receipts, including bonded trucking and airport feeder revenues invoiced in USD; all export receipts are freely held, netted, or transferred offshore without central-bank filing or authorization.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Not suitable for transactional treasury; development-finance facilities only

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital electronic-money institutions are not banks under the Banking Act 1991 and may not accept deposits or conduct treasury services inside the RMI; they are usable only as a supplementary low-value disbursement rail where the EMI segregates settlement funds in a licensed US or RMI correspondent account, and the Banking Commissioner remains likely to treat opaque EMI agent networks as an unacceptable AML/CFT concentration risk for this Customs Bonded Truck Fleet treasury profile.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is the default: at least one director and every beneficial owner above 10% must attend a KYC interview at BMI or the Bank of Guam Majuro branch, present the RMI corporate register certificate, business licence, and Customs Bonded Carrier licence, and sign the account mandate before a bank officer. Remote opening is granted only by risk override, requiring apostilled corporate records, notarized specimen signatures, a video interview with the bank's compliance officer, and a clearing-bank reference letter from a FATF-member jurisdiction; it is not available as a statutory right.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident Business Corporation lacking physical substance and local operating licences in RMI
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, Registered Agent acknowledgment, RMI Business Licence, Customs Bonded Carrier licence endorsed to ISIC 5222 road-feeder scope, audited interim accounts showing airport gateway contracts, and board resolution fixing treasury signatories and economic purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or nominee-controlled beneficial ownership, including any bearer-share or trust overlay
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully populated share register, RMI UBO declaration under Banking Act 1991 and the Money Laundering (Prevention and Control) Act 2000, sworn legal opinion confirming absence of outstanding bearer certificates or custodial ambiguity, and disclosure of any trust/nominee links with source-of-wealth evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds mismatch in the initial USD capital injection or subsequent intercompany funding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed bonded-feedering service agreement with an airline or freight-forwarding anchor client, pro-forma invoices, equity subscription or intercompany loan agreement, upstream bank confirmation of funds origin, and 12-month bank statements of each subscribing owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty or route nexus with sanctions lists, PEP status, or heightened-money-laundering-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-flow blueprint covering every feeder route and airport hub, OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening outputs for all owners and key counterparties, PEP declaration with negative-news narrative, sealed counterparty contracts, and a binding quarterly AML/CFT compliance-review covenant appointing an RMI-licensed compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital and intercompany loans are routed as USD-denominated SWIFT MT103 wires over Fedwire/CHIPS to the RMI collector bank, entering before the 14:00 Fedwire same-day cut-off. The wire narrative must cite the board resolution number and use purpose codes 'CAPT' for capital contribution or 'COL' for intercompany advance, mirrored on the bank's funds-origin checklist; the deposit is credited to the capital escrow sub-ledger against a documented share-allotment or loan agreement and is released for operational deployment only after the bank's compliance acceptance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational exits use USD SWIFT MT103 for fuel, driver payroll, landing/trucking gate fees, customs guarantees, and lessor payments, cleared via the bank's US correspondent over CHIPS with 48-to-72-hour settlement assurance; procurement of tractors, trailers, security seals, and GPS telematics above USD 250,000 is to be disbursed by a standby or commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700 / MT707 amendment cycle) with documents checked per UCP600; RMI has no domestic RTGS, so liquidity is staged against US market hours and the bank maintains an intraday USD liquidity buffer equal to 25% of monthly outbound commitments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable forwards in USD/AUD and USD/NZD under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a licensed RMI or US bank counterparty, tenor-matched to the bonded-trucking contract pipeline
Cross-currency swaps for long-horizon AUD/NZD lease and capital-expenditure liabilities, booked only to the treasury account and limited to notional exposures evidenced by existing purchase orders

Non-deliverable forwards (USD/IDR, USD/PHP, USD/VND) executed through a FATF-member offshore bank, net-settled in USD, maintained separately from the operational balance sheet to avoid speculative accounting treatment
Plain-vanilla purchased (long) FX options used solely to protect airport revenue conversions, with a firm prohibition on writing uncovered options under the RMI domestic banks' prudent-risk policies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Securities and Exchange Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before April 30 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of US$100 per month or fraction thereof; continued delinquency may lead to administrative strike-off and loss of good standing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit for non-resident business corporations; audit is compulsory only if shares are listed on a recognized exchange or if the corporation operates in a regulated financial sector
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No prescribed statutory framework; IFRS or US GAAP commonly used for internal and creditor-facing financial statements

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Marshall Islands has no public UBO register; the annual report confirms the registered office, registered agent, directors, and officers. Beneficial shareholding changes are not filed publicly but must be reflected in the corporation's internal register of members

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$500 – US$1,500 typical annual registered agent and registered office fee
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required for non-resident BC; if voluntarily audited for commercial purposes, US$3,000 – US$8,000 typical

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% – non-resident Business Corporations are fully exempt from Marshall Islands corporate income tax on all income, including foreign-source income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Complete statutory exemption from income tax; no capital gains tax, no branch profits tax, no alternative minimum tax. The only recurring mandatory government cost is the annual registration/franchise tax assessed under the Business Corporations Act (BCCA). Loss carryforward is conceptually inapplicable because the zero-tax regime creates no assessable tax base.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return is required for a non-resident Business Corporation in the Marshall Islands. The only annual compliance filing is the BCCA Annual Report and Franchise Tax Payment, administered by the Registrar of Corporations through the official online registry portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; no quarterly corporate income tax instalments or declarations apply.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The BCCA Annual Report and Franchise Tax payment are due on the anniversary date of incorporation. There is no CIT statutory deadline because the entity derives no taxable income in the Republic.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered corporate name, registration number, and financial year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact name from the Articles of Incorporation and clearly mark the entity as a non-resident Business Corporation to preserve the tax exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, physical address, and contact details of the licensed Marshall Islands resident agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A licensed resident agent is mandatory; the agent must be authorized to accept service of process and government notices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total number of authorized shares used as the basis for calculating the annual franchise tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the share schedule from the corporate charter; the franchise tax scales with authorized share count.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification that the company does not carry on any trade or business in the Marshall Islands.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This declaration confirms zero-rate CIT status and requires re-verification annually to avoid unintended local taxable presence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the BCCA Annual Report or to pay the franchise tax triggers a default notice, late-payment surcharges, and eventual administrative dissolution by the Registrar. No CIT late-filing penalty applies because no CIT return is owed for a fully exempt non-resident BC.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% – the Marshall Islands does not impose dividend withholding tax on distributions to shareholders, whether resident or non-resident.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Marshall Islands has no comprehensive double taxation agreement network; therefore, no treaty-relief procedure or Marshall Islands tax residency certificate is obtainable for local-tax purposes. If the shareholder is tax-resident in another jurisdiction, that jurisdiction may grant foreign tax credit under its domestic rules, but no Marshall Islands WHT is available to be credited because none is levied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 0% on royalties and interest paid to non-residents. Treaty rate: not applicable due to absence of a DTA network. Since no Marshall Islands withholding tax is levied on outbound interest or IP royalties, no administrative relief mechanism is required.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable – the Marshall Islands imposes no local transfer-pricing documentation thresholds, no Local File or Master File requirement, and no contemporaneous TP documentation duty for non-resident Business Corporations.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Marshall Islands has not enacted standalone Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to those of OECD-cooperative offshore centres. However, a non-resident BC must maintain its non-resident character by avoiding local business activity. Full economic substance and arm's-length pricing must instead be demonstrated in the jurisdictions where the GPS-sealed bonded trucking operation and airport logistics activities actually generate taxable profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the bonded truck-fleet business in a foreign taxing jurisdiction while using non-resident Marshall Islands formalities to evade foreign corporate income tax, or falsely declaring non-resident status while deriving income from Marshall Islands sources.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of the statutory income-tax exemption; administrative dissolution; monetary surcharges; disqualification from any future preferential treatment; and increased scrutiny by foreign tax authorities, which may disregard the Marshall Islands entity as a sham under foreign anti-avoidance rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false non-resident declarations can face piercing of the corporate veil, personal civil restitution for unpaid foreign taxes, and criminal prosecution for fraud in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Violation / Failure to File
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain a licensed registered agent, non-payment of the annual franchise tax, or repeated omission of the BCCA Annual Report while continuing to maintain bank accounts, execute contracts, and deploy the customs-bonded truck fleet.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Default notice, late fees, administrative strike-off and dissolution of the company with loss of separate legal personality; reinstatement only through extraordinary petition and payment of all arrears.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may become personally liable for company debts incurred after dissolution and may face director disqualification, travel restrictions, and civil claims by creditors and counterparties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the customs-bonded trucking operation to transport or facilitate the movement of proceeds of crime, evading customs controls, or dealing with sanctioned persons or entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalties, seizure and forfeiture of the truck fleet and banking assets, suspension or permanent revocation of the customs bonded licence, and criminal imprisonment under Marshall Islands anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual directors and officers can be arrested, personally fined, and imprisoned; the corporate veil is pierced for intentional money laundering and connected fraud; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed by the competent authorities.
